title: VPC/On‑Prem Networking Upgrade Roadmap — experiment log and runbook
content:
Purpose:
This document is a combined experiment log, runbook, and Terraform module notes for the planned VPC / on‑prem networking upgrade. The primary goals are: reduce per‑token egress cost by consolidating NAT paths, improve availability for private DNS resolution across hybrid clusters, and standardize firewall/network policy naming and test procedures for safe rollouts.

Scope and non‑goals:
- Scope: private deployments (VPC and on‑prem), focusing on DNS resolution (split‑horizon, conditional forwarding), ingress/egress topology, NAT design, firewall rules naming and migration, and Kubernetes network policies.
- Non‑goals: LB layer redesign, storage networking, or customer data model changes.

Quick summary of recommended approach (tl;dr):
1) Introduce a dual‑egress topology: local egress proxies in each colo + regional NAT gateway cluster for burst and centralized egress accounting.
2) Convert CoreDNS to explicit stub domains with TLS‑forwarding to egress proxies for external zones; keep internal zones served by on‑prem authoritative servers using conditional forwarders.
3) Use Terraform module versioned rollout with provider aliasing to allow staged apply across cloud and on‑prem resources; migrate state with terraform state mv during canary.
4) Enforce firewall and k8s network policy naming conventions and zero‑trust defaults; provide canary policy set for each namespace.

Architectural notes and decisions (short):
- Decision: prefer path-preserving SNAT (where possible) with source IP preservation to support license systems that rely on client IPs; fall back to full SNAT in high‑scale NAT cluster.
- Decision: prefer application-aware egress proxies (TLS inspection disabled by default) over ad‑hoc NAT for observability (metrics/trace tagging).
- Decision: implement split DNS via conditional forwarders + modified CoreDNS configmap in clusters.

Experiment log (chronological highlights):
- 2025-11-14: proof-of-concept: CoreDNS stubDomains + forward plugin to internal DNS worked for dev cluster; observed 30ms average extra lookup only when forwarding to remote authoritative.
- 2025-12-02: tested dual egress in lab: traffic to 3rd‑party model bucket successfully re-routed through regional NAT cluster under load; observed 12% lower token egress cost when batching/connection reuse enabled.
- 2026-01-08: created Terraform module variant with provider aliasing; ran a dry-run to create placeholder cloud NACLs and on‑prem ACLs (no traffic changes). Found provider conflict when modules referenced default provider—fixed by explicit provider_alias var.
- 2026-02-10: canary on staging: introduced firewall rule naming convention (fw-pvt-<team>-<env>-<purpose>) and validated audit logs integration.

Terraform module notes (practical):
- Module interface (recommended vars):
  - var.env (string)
  - var.team (string)
  - var.egress_mode ("local" | "regional" | "hybrid")
  - var.provider_alias_cloud (string)
  - var.provider_alias_onprem (string)
  - var.dns_forwarders (list(string))
  - var.firewall_rule_set (map) // flatten in caller to avoid nested complex types

- Provider alias usage pattern: always reference aws.with(alias = var.provider_alias_cloud) or onprem.provider.with(alias = var.provider_alias_onprem) so we can apply cloud and onprem parts independently. Avoid implicit default providers inside modules.

- State migration caveats: when renaming resources (eg change module path), run `terraform state mv` in a maintenance window. Suggested sequence:
  1) `terraform plan` on old module to capture state baseline.
  2) Add new module copy (no apply) in separate workspace, import minimal resource placeholders if required.
  3) `terraform state mv` old_resource new_module_resource
  4) Apply new module with `-target` to reconcile drift.
  5) Roll back by moving state back and applying old module if errors occur.

Firewall and naming conventions (must follow):
- Name pattern: fw-pvt-<team>-<env>-<direction>-<purpose>-<seq>
  - Examples: fw-pvt-sre-prod-egress-dns-01, fw-pvt-platform-staging-ingress-app-02
- Rule metadata: include owner tag, runbook link, and Jira ticket in description.
- Minimal rule set for baseline cluster (deny-by-default):
  - Allow DNS to internal resolvers (udp/53, tcp/53) from pod CIDRs to DNS servers
  - Allow egress to egress proxies (tcp/443) with TLS SNI tag in logs
  - Allow healthcheck ports from monitoring VPCs
  - Block all other 0.0.0.0/0 egress for privileged namespaces (enforce through CNI/NW policy)

Kubernetes network policy recommendations (Calico compatible):
- Default deny for ingress and egress at namespace level.
- Namespace label: network-zone: private or network-zone: public.
- Egress policy examples (text):
  - allow egress to kube-dns (service) for all pods in namespace
  - allow egress to egress-proxy service for trusted workloads
  - allow egress to ocsp/metadata endpoints for cert renewals only for infra namespaces

CoreDNS / Private DNS configuration notes:
- Use stubDomains in CoreDNS: example for cluster CoreDNS ConfigMap snippet (conceptual):
  - example.org: { forward . 10.10.2.2 10.10.2.3 tls_servername example.int }
- For split-horizon internal zones, configure conditional forwarders on on‑prem authoritative server to point at cloud VPC DNS forwarder and vice versa; document TTLs and expected propagation.
- Important: avoid chained forwarding loops; ensure each zone has a single forwarder target list with health checks.

Ingress / Egress flow patterns and failure modes considered:
- Pattern A: Local egress only — low latency, limited sharing of IPs, more NAT resources. Failure: if local egress proxies fail, pods lose external access.
- Pattern B: Regional NAT cluster — fewer public IPs, centralized observability, easier cost tracking. Failure: regional NAT cluster overload causes wholesale external failures.
- Hybrid: prefer hybrid — traffic defaults local, overflow or specific endpoints routed to regional NAT via routing policy.
- Failure mitigation: BGP anycast for egress proxies + health‑based routing to avoid blackhole. Also build automatic fallback in the routing layer to switch pod route table to regional NAT subnet if local proxy fails.

Testing and canary plan (phases):
- Phase 0: Unit tests for Terraform modules + plan gating in CI.
- Phase 1 (lab): deploy modules to isolated lab VPC and mini‑onprem. Validate CoreDNS forwarding, simple egress flows.
- Phase 2 (staging canary): roll out to one staging cluster (single namespace). Run synthetic workloads hitting external model buckets and telemetry endpoints.
- Phase 3 (customer canary): pick one low‑risk customer deployment for hybrid egress; run with double‑write logs to both old and new paths.
- Phase 4 (gradual rollout): rollout region by region with monitoring thresholds for latency, error rate, and egress throughput.

Rollout verification checks (smoke tests):
- DNS: resolved internal zone names correctly from pod and from host (expected IP ranges).
- Egress: curl https://model-bucket.example/ should succeed and show X-Forwarded-For header (if proxy path).
- NAT: for SNAT mode verify source IP is expected (use curl to echo service) and that sticky sessions preserve SRC when required.
- Firewall: check denied packets are logged and accepted ones have correct rule tag in logs.
- Metrics: verify no significant increase in p50/p95 latency for application endpoints (<= +10% allowed).

Rollback plan (if rollout fails):
1) Immediately mark canary cluster as maintenance.
2) Reconfigure route table to point pods back to legacy egress (or re-enable old proxy).
3) `terraform apply` to revert module changes (state preserved) or use state rollback if necessary.
4) Postmortem and revert of module refactor in git if root cause is module bug.

Operational runbook snippets (commands):
- Validate CoreDNS config: `kubectl -n kube-system get configmap coredns -o yaml` and `kubectl exec -n default busybox -- nslookup internal.example.org`
- Check egress proxy health: `curl -I https://egress-proxy.internal/healthz`
- Move Terraform resource state (example): `terraform state mv module.old.aws_nat_gateway.example module.new.aws_nat_gateway.example`

Open questions and risks to track (short list):
- Will customers with strict egress source IP requirements accept hybrid SNAT behavior? Need customer communications and opt‑in.
- Can on‑prem firewalls support dynamic health checks from cloud for forwarder failover? If not, we need manual failover runbooks.
- Cost sensitivity: regional NAT cluster reduces IP count but may increase data transfer costs; run cost model.

Next steps (action items):
- [ ] Finalize Terraform module interface and publish v0.1 with provider_alias pattern (owner: Ana) — target 2026-02-28.
- [ ] Create staging canary plan and schedule (owner: Jon) — target 2026-03-07.
- [ ] Prepare customer-facing note describing IP behavior changes and opt‑in path (owner: Leah) — target 2026-03-10.

Appendix A — Example Calico policy (flattened text):
apiVersion: projectcalico.org/v3
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-dns-and-egress-proxy
  namespace: example-namespace
spec:
  selector: all()
  types: ["Egress"]
  egress:
  - action: Allow
    destination:
      nets: ["10.10.0.0/16"] # kube-dns
  - action: Allow
    destination:
      selector: k8s-app == 'egress-proxy'

Appendix B — Example CoreDNS forward fragment (conceptual):
example.internal:53 {
    forward . 10.10.2.10 10.10.2.11
}

Notes: keep this doc as the living experiment log. Use the linked artifacts for formal runbooks and customer notices. When you update the module interface, append a numbered changelog entry at the top with date and brief rationale.
